clue.text: Part-timer shocks alluring women

parts.note: a temp is a temporary or part-time office worker
shocks of hair are tresses, long locks

explanation.surface: A part-time worker apparently electrifies some seductive women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocks' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: shocks of hair, i.e. tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Seductresses who lure men with their charms are synonymously called temptresses.

clue.text: Course record so modest at the outset

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: at the outset means only the opening letter of modest is used

explanation.surface: A racing record so modest at the start of a career.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a course, and Epsom Downs is a famous one.

clue.text: Oddly, despair spoken highly of

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of despair are arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: Strangely, a person in despair is nonetheless complimented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it signals rearranging all of DESPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spoken highly of is to be commended or lauded, a synonym.

clue.text: Stem river perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a stem sent out along the ground by a plant such as a strawberry
a river is something that runs, so cryptically one that runs

explanation.surface: Is the source of a river perhaps a kind of stem?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a river runs, so it might be called one that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal creeping plant shoot is a stolon; a river flows, i.e. runs.

clue.text: African very African!

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
a Malian is a person from Mali in Africa

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone being extremely African.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two jobs: the first gives a Mali native, the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is in the Horn of Africa, so someone or something from there is African.

clue.text: Vengeful Greek spoiled treacle

indicators.note: spoiled means the letters of treacle are ruined and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A vengeful Greek has ruined some syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Agamemnon's daughter helped avenge his murder by killing her mother Clytemnestra.

clue.text: Reported impertinence by those waiting for a haircut? Spicy stuff!

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is as heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: a line of customers at a hairdresser's is a barber queue
sauce is cheek or impertinence

explanation.surface: Waiting customers at the barber's give lip, and things get spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' covers only the barber's line; 'by' places the impertinence beside it. Queue is the British word for a line of people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangy condiment brushed on grilled meat is the spicy stuff in question.

clue.text: Solitary type, fellow struggling to carry on

indicators.note: to carry means the jumbled letters hold the next word inside them
struggling means the letters of fellow are in disarray and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A loner who is having a hard time keeping going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' looks like the solitary type himself, but it is anagram fodder: 'struggling' gives LEWOLF, which 'to carry' wraps round the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prefers to act alone, away from any group, is a loner of this kind.

clue.text: Comprehensive hit when everyone refuses to work

parts.note: general means widespread or comprehensive
to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A sweeping blow lands just as all workers down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a noun but works as the verb strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass walkout by workers across all industries is a national stoppage of labour.

clue.text: Confused when fishing, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: out on the ocean, as a trawler crew is when fishing

explanation.surface: Is someone bewildered while out angling?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for bewildered is also the literal phrase for being out on the ocean.

clue.text: Hit yourself

definitions.meaning: oneself, as in looking after one's own interests

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a chart-topping single and also, colloquially, one's own self.

clue.text: Weapon striking girl?

explanation.surface: A weapon is used to hit a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like a verb of violence but means stunningly attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an explosive shell and, colloquially, a sensationally attractive woman.

clue.text: The writer of this puzzle a subject for discussion

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter proposes himself as a topic for debate.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often calls themself me, I or setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic or main idea talked about is a synonym for subject of discussion.

clue.text: Something like a cricket cap is coveted, and delighting Australian openers

indicators.note: openers means the first letters of each word from cap to Australian

explanation.surface: A cricket cap is prized, to the joy of Australia's opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about the sport of cricket (and its openers, the first two batsmen); the definition means the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This chirping insect is related to and resembles a cricket or grasshopper.

clue.text: Store trophy on flat surface

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the trophy above the flat surface

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
a board is a flat surface

explanation.surface: Put your trophy away on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a verb but the answer is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet where things are kept is a place of storage, a store.

clue.text: Wine around South Africa certainly not for ladies' man

indicators.note: around means the wine encircles the other pieces

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
no is a firm refusal

explanation.surface: Wine taken round South Africa is definitely not for a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century Venetian adventurer is a byword for a seducer of women.

clue.text: Flower opened, a daisy's beginning to come up

indicators.note: to come up in a down clue means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lid off describes something opened

indicators.note: beginning means just the opening letter of daisy

explanation.surface: A daisy's flower opened and starts to come up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' reverses LIDOFFAD, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow spring bloom is a narcissus, a flower.

clue.text: Particular brewing of ales, epic

indicators.note: brewing means the letters of ales and epic are stirred together and rearranged

explanation.surface: A particular brew of ales is epic.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is an older form of special, meaning particular or exceptional.

clue.text: All the best encouragement I love

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A send-off with some heartening words of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheerio is a British informal goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal farewells, a parting wish for good luck.

clue.text: County provides employees

definitions.meaning: short for Staffordshire, an English Midlands county
supplies with workers, as a verb

explanation.surface: A county council supplies the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands, often shortened this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The county name is commonly abbreviated, and the verb means supplies with personnel.

clue.text: Swimmer touring islands and one country

indicators.note: touring means the fish travels around the other pieces

parts.note: a tuna is a fish, a swimmer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A swimmer makes a tour of several islands and one country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: An official in college on the range

parts.note: a dean is a senior college official

explanation.surface: A college administrator is out on the mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The range is the Andes mountains of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of or belonging to the Andes, the great South American mountain chain.

clue.text: A flower came to light

parts.note: a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A flower appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To have arisen or emerged is to have come to light, the past tense of arise.

clue.text: Money man in more ostentatious clothes

indicators.note: clothes, as a verb, means the fancier word dresses round the other one

parts.note: fancier means showier, more ostentatious

explanation.surface: A wealthy man wearing flashier outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but works as a verb meaning wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker or investor who handles large sums is a money man.

clue.text: Clubs I initially rely on, not spades

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each word from I to spades

explanation.surface: A card player relies on clubs, not spades.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about card suits, but the clubs are golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs with metal heads and angled faces are called by this metal's name.

clue.text: Move top article in magazine

parts.note: to cart is to move or carry
a ridge is the top, as of a roof

explanation.surface: Shift the leading story in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a periodical; it is the ammunition chamber of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A round of ammunition is loaded into a firearm's magazine, so it is an item there.

clue.text: Ordinary wares

definitions.meaning: goods held for sale by a shop

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means standard or usual; as a noun it means goods kept for sale.

clue.text: Rich yellow food in salad stuffed in mouth, perhaps?

indicators.note: the second in means the jumbled letters go inside the opening

parts.note: a hole is an opening, a mouth being an example

indicators.note: stuffed means the letters of in salad are messed up, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A rich yellow dressing in a salad, crammed into the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This butter and egg-yolk emulsion is a rich yellow sauce.
